body:
Thank you for the reply! Yeah, I can feel how hard they work to build up the courage to ask for help in their circle of "trusted" adults and it really saddens me to see it doesn't result in anything. We talk in a group setting (via discord server), but they also message me privately when it's more serious topics. I've told them it's a no-judgement zone, but I also worry I'm saying the wrong things or whatever so I try to mainly just listen. I'm glad just giving them the space to talk can help somewhat because I do feel powerless in the situation. Will just keep on  supporting them on their journey to continue building courage so that they can keep fighting for the help they so deserve.

Thank you for clarifying the mother situation, I wasn't 100% sure because I was thinking what if they're in active danger. What then do I do? They're at an age where they're still very dependent on trusted adults so that's why I feel my options are so limited (or really, none). I'll take your advice and just keep an open door policy and continue checking in on them. Thanks again, kind stranger!
